subject: Follow-up: deployment isolation matrix & noisy-neighbor guarantees
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@medline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment isolation matrix & noisy-neighbor guarantees

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks so we can produce an isolation recommendation tailored to MedLine Health: 

- High-level ask: you mentioned concern about noisy-neighbor interference for your critical triage workflows and a need for SLA guarantees around tail latency for the patient-facing inference endpoint.
- Minimum SLO: you said 99th percentile inference latency target of ~200ms at 512 tokens for the peak hour.
- Workload shape: per our notes, typical sustained QPS ~60 with spiky bursts to ~220 for a few minutes during peak.
- Data requirements: PHI-only in the inference path, logs retained for 90 days, and customer-managed keys for model inputs/outputs.

To make progress we need three quick items from you:
1) Confirm the sustained QPS / burst numbers above or send a short daily peak table.
2) Confirm whether you require tenant-level physical isolation (dedicated capacity) or just stronger soft-isolation (priority routing + reserved slots) — I can draw up a simple isolation matrix either way.
3) Any additional compliance gating (SOC2 evidence, data residency region, customer KMS provider) beyond what we covered.

Attached is a one-sheet 'SLO primer' that explains how we measure tail latency and a blank isolation-matrix template — if you fill the table we can map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private recommendations.

Proposed next steps: once we have the filled matrix we'll schedule a short technical alignment (30m) with Ben (runtime) and Marissa (eng ops) to scope a POC. Would Wednesday morning (PST) or Thursday afternoon work for you?

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: isolation-matrix-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-slo-primer.pdf (doc)
From: Anna Park <anna@medline.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@medline.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment isolation matrix & noisy-neighbor guarantees

Logan —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline: 

- QPS: sustained ~55–65 QPS during normal operation; predictable daily spike window 08:30–09:15 PST that can hit ~200–240 QPS for 6–8 minutes. Nighttime batch jobs add a short sustained 120 QPS window at 02:00–02:15 PST.
- SLO: yes, 99th <= 200ms at 512 tokens is the internal target for the triage product and non-negotiable for an MVP go-live. If you have data on how Dedicated vs Hosted impacts tail latency, that would be helpful.
- Isolation preference: security has asked us to prioritize a solution that minimizes blast radius for the first 12 months. That pushes us toward Dedicated capacity in the near term, but procurement will need a cost/benefit run and we might accept a hosted+reserved-slot approach if the measured tail-latency is within SLO and KMS integration is customer-controlled.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report and a statement on key handling (HSM/KMS) are required. Data residency: US only.

I'll fill the matrix and return it by end of day tomorrow. For the alignment call, Thursday 2027-07-29 at 11:00 AM PST works for Ben/Marissa and our infra lead.

Anna Park
Director, Platform Engineering | MedLine Health
anna@medline.ai

>

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment isolation matrix & noisy-neighbor guarantees

Anna / team —

Great — thanks for the numbers and the compliance checklist. A few short notes so the Thursday call is productive: 

- Based on the burst profile you provided (200–240 QPS for short windows), our runtime team recommends a Dedicated capacity baseline for the MVP if the 99th <= 200ms is required. Dedicated lets us reserve GPU pools, pin model variants, and enforce hard CPU/GPU resource boundaries which materially reduce head-of-line and tail latency variance.
- If you decide to try Hosted + reserved slots initially, we recommend a 2-week calibration POC: run the workload on Hosted with prefix caching and KV pinning, and measure 99th latency at the same traffic profile. If that fails to meet the SLO we can convert to Dedicated with a migration playbook we keep ready.
- For KMS: we can integrate with AWS KMS customer-managed keys or bring-your-own HSM for Private deployments; Dedicated supports CMK-per-tenant for encryption at rest and in transit keys for log exporters. We'll bring our security engineer to the call to run through the exact artifacts you need for SOC 2.

Action items before Thursday:
1) Anna: matrix populated (you mentioned EOD tomorrow) — we'll validate and map to our recommendation.
2) Logan: prepare a short calibration plan (baseline test on Hosted + reserved slots) and a Dedicated runbook with migration steps and estimated lead time.
3) Marissa: prepare rough cost delta numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated for the expected QPS pattern so procurement has a ballpark.

We'll use the HubSpot deal DL-9347 to track procurement asks and I'll upload the SOC 2 checklist. See you Thursday 11:00 AM PST.

Thanks —

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
